findings.fix: Collect the house number and street together in one address-line field.
findings.violation: The house number has its own field separate from the street, and it is required, so an address with no number cannot be entered.

findings.fix: Replace it with the standard token for this field, for example email.
findings.violation: The autocomplete value e-mail is not a valid autofill detail in the HTML standard, so autofill is broken for this field.

findings.evidence: <label id="website-label" for="website-input">Company website</label> <input id="website-input" name="website" type="url" required=""> on a form headed 'Create your account' / 'Create your Meridian Outfitters account', with no other field or heading indicating a business or company-account task.
findings.fix: Remove the field, or make it optional and relevant only on a business-account path, separate from the plain account sign-up.
findings.violation: Creating a personal retail account does not need a company website, and the field is required and typed url, so a browser will reject anything that is not a well-formed URL. A person with no company and no website has no valid value to supply and cannot finish the form.

findings.evidence: <button id="viewdetails-btn" type="button" style="padding:12px 20px;font-size:16px">View details</button> sits between the row-contacttime field and the row-hear field, while the unstyled primary submit <button id="submit-btn" type="submit">Submit</button> sits only after the last field, row-hear.
findings.fix: Move the 'View details' control out of the field sequence, such as beside the primary submit or elsewhere outside the column of fields, and style it as visibly secondary to Submit.
findings.violation: A secondary, non-submitting action is placed among the fields rather than beside the primary action where the fields end, and it carries explicit padding and font-size styling while the primary submit carries none, so it reads as at least as prominent as the button that actually finishes the form.

findings.fix: Label the button with the action it performs, such as Create account or Send message.
findings.violation: The form's primary button is labelled Submit, a generic word that says nothing about what pressing it does.
On this name field, autocorrection and spellchecking stay on, so a phone keyboard can change a value it does not know.

findings.fix: Remove the confirmation field and offer a control that shows the password as typed.
findings.violation: The form asks for the new password a second time to confirm it, doubling the typing for every person.

findings.evidence: <label id="contacttime-label" for="contacttime-input" style="display:block">Preferred contact time</label> <input id="contacttime-input" name="contact_time" type="text" required="">.
findings.fix: Remove the field from account sign-up and ask it later, in the flow where a contact time is actually used.
findings.violation: Account creation does not need a preferred contact time; nothing on the form uses it at this step, and it could be asked later, only when the business actually needs to schedule contact.
